acip: RKANG PA DANG PO GNYIS NI SMON 'JUG GNYIS KYI DON BSDU DANG , DE NAS GNYIS NI SDOM PA LNGA'I DON BSDU'O, ,MA GROL PA NI GTI MUG SOGS SGRIB PA GNYIS KYI 'CHING BAS BCINGS PA'I TSANGS PA LA SOGS PA STE DE RNAMS DGROL BA DANG NYAN RANG SHES SGRIB LAS MA BRGAL BA RNAMS DE LAS BSGRAL BA DANG , DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA DBUGS MA PHYIN PA RNAMS DBUGS DBYUNG ZHING SEMS CAN KUN MI GNAS PA'I MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA LA DGOD DO ZHES PA NI MAN SNYE DANG RDO RJE MKHA' 'GRO'I RNAM BSHAD GNYIS KA'I DGONGS PA'O, ,TSIGS BCAD THA MA 'DI 'JUG SEMS BSKYED PA LA MAN SNYER BSHAD DO,
wylie: rkang pa dang po gnyis ni smon 'jug gnyis kyi don bsdu dang , de nas gnyis ni sdom pa lnga'i don bsdu'o, ,ma grol pa ni gti mug sogs sgrib pa gnyis kyi 'ching bas bcings pa'i tshangs pa la sogs pa ste de rnams dgrol ba dang nyan rang shes sgrib las ma brgal ba rnams de las bsgral ba dang , dmyal ba la sogs pa dbugs ma phyin pa rnams dbugs dbyung zhing sems can kun mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa la dgod do zhes pa ni man snye dang rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i rnam bshad gnyis ka'i dgongs pa'o, ,tshigs bcad tha ma 'di 'jug sems bskyed pa la man snyer bshad do
english: The first four lines [in the English] here summarize the meaning of the Wish for enlightenment, in both the form of a prayer, and action.  The next two lines summarize the five vows. The words "those who have yet to be freed" refer to beings such as the Pure One, Brahma, who are still bound in the fetters of ignorance and so on: the two kinds of obstacles; and we commit to free them. "Those who have yet to be saved" refers to those of the ways of listeners and self-made Buddhas, who are yet to be saved from the obstacles to omniscience; we commit to save them. "Those who have no comfort" is a reference to beings such as those in the realms of hell; we are resolving to bring them comfort.  And we decide finally to deliver all living beings to a state of nirvana which is beyond both of the extremes.  This is how both the Golden Harvest and the Explication of the Angel of Diamond both interpret these lines.  The Golden Harvest further explains the final verse as referring to the Wish for enlightenment in the form of action. ***
